THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Fast Food Breakfast Tacos

41g protein, 403 cal, 8 minutes. The fast-food drive-through equivalent — built at home.

YIELD1 serving
TOTAL TIME8 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~403 cal | ~41g protein

Ingredients

TIER 2 PROTEIN STACK (this is the 41g)

  • 2 large eggs (~140 cal, 12g protein)
  • 1 serving 365 Organic Black Forest Uncured Ham, fine-diced (~70 cal, 11g protein)
  • 1 serving Kraft Fat Free Shredded Cheddar (~45 cal, 9g protein)

TIER 4 FRESHNESS (recommended — kills the beige)

  • 1-2 tbsp pickled red onion OR fresh cilantro (pick one, not both)

TIER 3 CARB (the enabler)

  • 3 Mission Zero Net Carbs Original tortillas (small/street-taco size, ~110 cal total, 7g protein)

TIER 1 SIGNATURE SAUCE (the MVP — turns 'fitness food' into 'fast food')

  • 1 serving Smoky Chipotle Crema (~38-40 cal, 2g protein)

COOKING

  • Cooking spray or 1 tsp butter for the scramble pan
  • Pinch of salt

You want the experience of a drive-through breakfast taco run — handheld, melty, sauced — without the calories or the wait. 41g protein at 403 cal beats anything on the McD's value menu by 20g protein and saves you $8.

Method

  1. 1.WARM TORTILLAS FIRST. Stack 3 Mission Zero tortillas, wrap in a damp paper towel, microwave 10 seconds. OR pass each over an open gas flame 5 sec/side for char. Stiff cold tortillas = the #1 reason these taste like fitness food. Don't skip.
  2. 2.FINE-DICE THE HAM. Cut into pieces smaller than your fingernail. Big chunks distribute unevenly — fine dice means every bite gets ham. This is the difference between 'home cooking' and 'craveable fast food'.
  3. 3.SOFT SCRAMBLE. Crack 2 eggs into a small bowl, whisk with a pinch of salt. Heat a nonstick pan on MEDIUM-LOW (not medium, not high), spray with cooking spray. Add eggs. Pull them slowly across the pan with a spatula — you want creamy, slightly underdone curds, not dry chunks. Off heat at 80% set — they finish from carryover. ~90 seconds total.
  4. 4.ADD HAM + CHEESE TO PAN. Off heat, fold in the diced ham + 1 serving Kraft FF cheddar. Residual heat melts the cheese into the egg without overcooking it.
  5. 5.ASSEMBLE. Divide the scramble across the 3 warm tortillas. Don't dump — distribute evenly.
  6. 6.SAUCE THE RIGHT WAY. From a squeeze bottle, draw a thin ZIGZAG of Smoky Chipotle Crema across each taco. Not a dump in the middle.
  7. 7.GREEN HIT. Pinch of pickled red onion OR chopped cilantro across all three. This is what kills the beige-on-beige problem and makes the plate look intentional instead of desperate. Skip it and you've made fitness food.
  8. 8.EAT HANDHELD. Fold and bite. Eat within 60 sec — Mission Zero tortillas crack if they sit assembled and cold.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid: Serve the kid portion as described above.

If something fails

Tortillas crack when folding: Cold or under-warmed. Damp paper towel + microwave 10 sec, OR open flame 5 sec/side. Stiff tortillas are the most common failure mode here.

Eggs are dry / rubbery: Heat too high or cooked too long. Medium-LOW, not medium. Pull off at 80% set — they finish from carryover heat.

Big ham chunks make some bites flavorful and others bland: Fine dice. Smaller than your fingernail. Distribute evenly across all 3 tacos before topping.

Looks like 'fitness food' in photos / on the plate: Three fixes, in order: (1) zigzag the sauce from a squeeze bottle, don't dump. (2) Add pickled red onion or cilantro — the green hit is non-negotiable for visual energy. (3) Warm the tortillas properly — pale stiff tortillas read as 'sad meal prep.'

Cheese clumps instead of melting smoothly: You added cheese while pan was still on heat — direct heat overcooks fat-free cheese into rubbery clumps. Off heat + residual warmth is the move.

Want more heat: Bump the Smoky Chipotle Crema portion to 1.5 servings, OR add a couple slices of pickled jalapeño on top. Don't sub a different sauce — the chipotle smoke IS the flavor identity here.

Storage and reheating

Store: Best fresh — 8 minutes to make. The crema lasts 5-7 days in fridge if you batched it.

Reheat: N/A — make fresh.

Lasts: N/A — eat immediately. Mission Zero tortillas crack if assembled tacos sit.

Adult plate | Kid plate

Adult plate

Adult

Full recipe as written — 3 tacos with chipotle drizzle + pickled red onion + cilantro garnish.

Kid plate

Kid

Scale down to 2 tacos. Skip the chipotle (mild Avocado Cilantro from /cookbook/umami-lemon-heat-style sauces works), and keep cheese melted on top instead of mixed in. Most kids will eat plain scrambled egg + cheese + ham in a tortilla.

Brands I use

Mission
Zero Net Carbs Original Tortillas (Street Taco Size)
Tier 3 carb — the enabler. 3 small tortillas for 110 cal + 7g protein. Without these, 'high-protein breakfast tacos' is a contradiction. Critics call them processed; reality is they unlock wraps, tacos, breakfast, pizza bases, quesadillas at controlled calories.
365 by Whole Foods Market
Organic Black Forest Uncured Ham
Tier 2 protein layer. 11g protein at 70 cal, clean ingredients, fine-dices easily. Pre-cooked = no extra pan.
Kraft
Fat Free Shredded Cheddar
Tier 2 protein layer. 9g protein at 45 cal — the trick is that fat-free shredded cheddar melts well under residual heat (not direct heat), which is why the recipe folds it in off-heat.
Smoky Chipotle Crema
Cookbook cross-link — the MVP sauce
Tier 1 signature sauce. Without it, this recipe is 'fitness food'. With it, it's craveable. Make a batch ahead (5-7 days fridge life, 12 servings) and you have the sauce for these tacos PLUS steak, bowls, tacos, wraps — ecosystem sauce.
